I set up the 20 experiments as 10 matched pairs. In each pair, both runs apply the same edit to parents that differ only in the condition being tested. The difference between the two results then isolates the interaction from the edit's average effect.

| Pair | Edit | Condition varied |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | edge 5 → nor_conv_3x3 | edge 1 is none (node 2 cut off) vs nor_conv_3x3 |
| 2 | edge 3 → skip_connect | edge 5 is nor_conv_3x3 vs none |
| 3 | edge 0 → nor_conv_3x3 | edge 4 is none (edge 0 unused) vs nor_conv_3x3 |
| 4 | edge 4 → none | edge 3 is skip_connect vs none |
| 5 | edge 1 → avg_pool_3x3 | replaces nor_conv_3x3 vs replaces none |
| 6 | edge 2 → skip_connect | edge 1 is nor_conv_3x3 vs none |
| 7 | edge 5 → avg_pool_3x3 | edge 3 is skip_connect vs avg_pool_3x3 |
| 8 | edge 3 → nor_conv_3x3 | edges 4 and 5 are none vs nor_conv_3x3 |
| 9 | edge 0 → none | edge 2 is nor_conv_3x3 vs none |
| 10 | edge 4 → nor_conv_1x1 | edge 0 is avg_pool_3x3 vs nor_conv_3x3 |
